why: A segment has a definite finite length, and exactly one point on it divides that length into two equal parts, so there is only one mid point.

Two distinct lines cannot share two points (two points determine a unique line, which would make them the same line), so they meet in at most one point — the intended answer is one, though strictly parallel distinct lines meet in no point, so the option set is arguably incomplete.
solution: Two distinct lines cannot pass through two common points, because Euclid's postulate says there is one and only one line through two points -- two shared points would make them the same line. So they meet in at most one point, and the answer is (C) one. [Note: if the two distinct lines are parallel they meet in NO point, so the fully general answer is 'one or none'. The options offer no such choice, and (C) is the intended answer -- compare Q.1 (iii), which does offer a case-covering option.]
